title: Most Majestic Game
reviewNotes: Most Majestic Game: eight selected variations checked from the position after Nc6 Kxc6; the preceding eight-piece setup is outside that tablebase check.
transcript: Knight to c7 is a beautiful sacrifice that has to be accepted because if black tries to run towards promotion, now there's going to be knight to b4 with a fork. White is going to collect the pawn and win the game. So, black just takes the knight and now we can realize that the position is not that straightforward. White does have a bishop, but black is only two steps away from getting a new queen. But white can continue with bishop to f6 and now again, if black tries to push, white would be able to collect this pawn and then stop the promotion. But of course, black can just defend the pawn. Not from here though. This would allow a skewer, but from this light square that doesn't allow the dark square bishop to actually interact with the king. The king is too far away to reach the pawn. So, is this it? Is black simply going to win in this position? Well, not exactly. White plays pawn to d3, a mysterious move allowing the pawn to push and reach the final square towards promotion. But white does have a brilliant idea in mind to win [music] this position. C4 check forces a reply by black. If black takes en passant, white is actually just going to collect this pawn, stop the promotion, and prevent the black king from collecting the white pawn. [music] And if the king moves away from the black pawn, white can still capture it. black has to play king to c5. And now, it seems like black is simply out of the woods. This pawn cannot be collected without losing the bishop. The queen is about to be summoned and the king is still too far away. But just when all hope seems [music] lost, black realizes that he's the one to be completely lost after the majestic king to b7. A move that doesn't seem to make sense. Can't black simply get a new queen? Well, as it turns out, white was preparing a mating [music] net because bishop to e7, out of nowhere, is checkmate.
